function: CSI feedback compression and reconstruction: learned encoder and CNN-regularized unfolded decoder (RE-LENet) applied to AR-prediction differential terms of time-varying channels (p. 2-3).
system: Massive MIMO FDD: BS with 32 antennas, single-antenna UE, 1024 subcarriers, 300 MHz carrier, UE at 60 km/h (QuaDRiGa Berlin UMa NLOS); no RIS (p. 1, 2, 4).
method: Supervised deep unfolding: learnable fully-connected compression layer plus six-CNN learned-regularization decoder unrolled for 6 iterations; MSE loss, Adam, 400 epochs (p. 3-4).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa dataset, BERLIN UMa NLOS outdoor, 300 MHz, 32 antennas, parameters as in [7]-[9]; 100000 training, 30000 validation, 20000 test samples; UE speed raised to 60 km/h (p. 4).
test_conditions: Split of one QuaDRiGa set at 60 km/h; also 90 km/h with T=5 and LMMSE-estimated CSI (15, 20 dB); training for 90 km/h not stated (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned only: ISTA-Net, ISTA-Net+, TiLISTA-joint, LORA, CsiNet Pro, ENet, CsiNet-LSTM, MarkovNet, MN-IE, DeepCMC, mu-CsiQNet; variants RM, AR-ISTA; no non-learned method (p. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE of initial channel and differential terms versus CR; NMSE per timeslot; convergence loss; NMSE versus feedback bit rate; parameters and FLOPs (p. 4-5).
complexity: Table IV: RE-LENet has 1.17M, 0.25M, 0.18M parameters and 244.04M, 240.37M, 240.11M FLOPs at CR 1/4, 1/32, 1/64 (p. 5).
openness: none; no code or data link (p. 1-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "We deploy QuaDRiGa to generate the simulation dataset"; Table I gives the BERLIN UMa NLOS model, 32 BS antennas and 300 MHz.
q2_support: p. 5: "when the speed increases to 90 km/h" the restart time is set to 5, but Table I (p. 4) trains at 60 km/h and the paper never says whether the 90 km/h case reuses or retrains the model.
q3_support: p. 4: "Fig. 4 presents the comparison of the proposed RE-LENet, ISTA-Net [12], ISTA-Net+ [9]"; every compared method (ISTA-type, LORA, CsiNet Pro, ENet, CsiNet-LSTM, MarkovNet, MN-IE, DeepCMC, mu-CsiQNet) is learned, and no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "Table IV exhibits the parameters and floating point operations (FLOPs) of various methods"; RE-LENet has 1.17M parameters and 244.04M FLOPs at CR = 1/4 (table read from the page image).
q5_support: p. 4: "We deploy QuaDRiGa to generate the simulation dataset"; the data are generated by the authors with a simulator, not a released dataset, and no code link, data link or DOI appears in the letter.
notes: Included as area 2 (CSI feedback). q1 is met through QuaDRiGa (BERLIN UMa NLOS), while q5 is not, since no dataset or code is released. q2 is borderline: the 90 km/h results of Table III (p. 5) may come from a model trained at 60 km/h, but the paper does not say so, and the LMMSE-estimated CSI test is only a CSI error sweep; the reviewer should check. q3: ISTA-Net, TiLISTA-joint and LORA are learned (deep unfolding), and no non-learned baseline appears in Figs. 4-7 (legends read from the page images). Tables I and IV were read from the page images. The order-2 AR predictor (Yule-Walker) is classical but part of the proposed framework.
